Zarichanka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Zarichanka — formerly known as Lanckoroń — was where Jacob Frank's Polish career began in the 1750s; in a private house here, his followers reportedly held a ritual in which a woman symbolized the Torah, an episode that became notorious in accounts of the Frankist movement, documented at several other towns in this collection. An organized Jewish community existed by the 16th century, growing to 1,893 (50 percent) by 1897, supporting five synagogues by 1913. The Jewish population of Zarichanka was deported to the Kamyanets-Podilskyi ghetto and executed there.
